prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: side impact at intersection in Houston, Texas. Injury: knee injury. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1104; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just say I'm the plaintiff in this case, if that's acceptable.
Q: That's fine for today, but I'll need your address and occupation before we finish. Let's talk about the accident. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was driving through an intersection in Houston, heading east on a main road with a green light.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the collision?
A: Not until the last second. A vehicle came from my right side and entered the intersection. I tried to brake, but there wasn't time.
Q: Which part of your vehicle was struck?
A: The driver's side door, right where I was sitting. The impact pushed my car sideways.
Q: Did you hit anything else after the impact?
A: No, the car came to rest against the curb on the far side of the intersection.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was.
Q: How did you feel immediately afterward?
A: Shaken, mostly. My left knee hurt right away, and it was hard to get out of the car without putting weight on it.
Q: Did you seek medical care that day?
A: An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They X-rayed the knee and wrapped it, then told me to follow up with an orthopedic doctor.
Q: Have you been to that orthopedic doctor?
A: Yes, I've been seeing them for several months now. I've had physical therapy twice a week and a few injections.
Q: How would you describe your knee now compared to before the accident?
A: Before, I ran a few times a week and had no problems. Now I can't run at all, and stairs are difficult, especially going down.
Q: How has this affected your daily life?
A: I had to stop coaching my nephew's soccer team because I can't stand for long periods. I also rely on my spouse for help with grocery shopping and carrying things.
Q: Have you missed any work?
A: I've taken time off for appointments and for a couple of flare-ups when the pain was too much to sit at my desk.
Q: Have you had any prior injuries to either knee?
A: No, not to my knowledge. My left knee had never given me trouble before this.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about how the accident has affected you?
A: Mostly that I'm frustrated. I used to be active without thinking about it, and now every day involves planning around my knee.
